findings.title: Rollback recovery ignores existing contradictory forward evidence
findings.observation: The new QUIESCING plus empty-live-project branch reconstructs PASS from the lifecycle alone without requiring forward-restore-cleanup.json to be absent or resolving it when present. executeRollbackWithCleanup calls cleanupOwnedProject directly for RESTORE, bypassing cleanupForwardRestoreProject's fixed-path parse and binding checks.
findings.trigger: Leave a RESTORE lifecycle in QUIESCING after deletion, then place a structurally and digest-valid forward-restore-cleanup.json whose restoreComposeProject conflicts with the actual project, or place malformed evidence, before actual rollback resumes.
findings.impact: The contradictory record is ignored; rollback writes a separate PASS aggregate, transitions the restore lifecycle to CLEANED with a rollback reference and emits terminal ROLLED_BACK. Durable evidence can therefore contain a conflicting source while the terminal state claims verified cleanup, contrary to the accepted unique-authority and fail-closed contract.

evidence.description: A review-only exact-head test wrote a digest-valid forward record bound to a different restore project, then called executeRollbackWithCleanup. The promise resolved terminal ROLLED_BACK instead of rejecting.
A fresh-context independent reviewer reproduced the same direct-rollback bypass and classified the evidence-presence gate as blocking.
The new recovery branch checks only scope, lifecycle state and live emptiness; actual rollback calls cleanupOwnedProject directly instead of the forward resolver.
The committed regression explicitly proves ENOENT before rollback, so it does not discriminate malformed, binding-conflicting or valid existing forward evidence.
The current design says conflicting evidence or identity remains a failure and existing valid records are re-read and returned as the same authority.

findings.remediation: Use the missing-evidence recovery only when the fixed forward-evidence path is absent. When it is present, parse and resolve it against the exact attempt, restore project, database and QUIESCING authority, reuse the exact persisted result if valid, and fail closed for malformed, wrong-bound or conflicting content before publishing rollback PASS.
findings.verification: Exercise the actual executeRollbackWithCleanup path for absent, valid matching, malformed and digest-valid wrong-project forward evidence. Only absent and valid matching evidence may reach ROLLED_BACK; valid evidence must be reused exactly, and every rejected case must produce no PASS aggregate or terminal ROLLED_BACK.

findings.observation: The current implementation detects only RESTORE QUIESCING with a nonempty frozen set and an empty exact live project, derives the same removal-argument digest from the frozen authority, then requires consecutive empty samples without issuing another delete.
findings.trigger: The process dies after completing the frozen restore deletion but before forward-restore-cleanup.json is written, then actual rollback resumes with no forward evidence.
findings.impact: The prior safe-but-unrecoverable empty state now completes to PASS, CLEANED and terminal ROLLED_BACK rather than CLEANUP_FAILED and ROLLBACK_FAILED.
